_meta.description: Deprecated CPython C APIs that CPython's OWN code still calls. Backs scan_deprecated_apis.py.
_meta.method: Every entry was checked against the tree itself: Py_DEPRECATED / _Py_DEPRECATED_EXTERNALLY markers in Include/, `.. deprecated::` / `.. soft-deprecated::` directives in Doc/c-api/, and Doc/deprecations/c-api-pending-removal-in-*.rst. Nothing here is from memory.

tiers.hard: Py_DEPRECATED(...) marker in Include/. The compiler warns for external users AND for CPython's own build.
tiers.hard-internal: _Py_DEPRECATED_EXTERNALLY(...) marker. Include/pyport.h:269-274 expands this to NOTHING under Py_BUILD_CORE, so -Wdeprecated-declarations is silent on CPython's own call sites. A scanner is the only way to find these -- this is the highest-value tier.
tiers.soft: Documented as deprecated / soft-deprecated but carrying no compiler marker.

_meta.severity_rule: removed_in set -> FIX (the call will stop compiling in that release). Otherwise CONSIDER.

schema.drop_in: true when `replacement` is a mechanical substitution. FALSE means applying the named replacement changes behaviour -- read `caveat` before migrating. This field exists because a scanner that confidently recommends a regression is worse than one that stays silent: the single FIX of the Modules/ run was _PyUnicodeWriter_WriteStr, whose named replacement reintroduces gh-148241.
schema.caveat: What breaks if the replacement is applied mechanically, and the verified drop-in to use instead. Required when drop_in is false.
schema.compat_shim_files: Repo-relative files where a use of this API is the API's own backwards-compatibility implementation, its definition, or a test that exercises it deliberately. Suppressed as ACCEPTABLE rather than reported -- without this the 21 Py_*Flag globals would land ~60 findings in Python/initconfig.c and Python/preconfig.c and look like the old scanner's definition-site problem returning.

_meta.drop_in_rule: drop_in: false REQUIRES a non-empty caveat. A replacement whose name contains Ref/Frame/New is suspect by construction: the PEP 667 family (PyEval_GetGlobals/Builtins/Locals) all returned STRONG references where the deprecated call returns BORROWED, and all three shipped as drop_in: true with an empty caveat. That is the second time this class of error reached a recommendation -- the first nearly reintroduced gh-148241, which is why these fields exist.

apis.name: _PyUnicodeWriter_Init
apis.notes: Include/cpython/unicodeobject.h:554. Suppressed under Py_BUILD_CORE, so CPython's own ~19 call sites compile silently.

apis.name: _PyUnicodeWriter_WriteStr
apis.caveat: PyUnicodeWriter_WriteStr() is NOT a drop-in: it tests `type == &PyUnicode_Type` EXACTLY (Objects/unicode_writer.c:364), so a str subclass falls through to PyObject_Str(obj) and runs a user __str__ -- that was gh-148241, and Modules/_json.c:407 carries a comment saying so two lines above the call. The verified drop-in is PyUnicodeWriter_WriteSubstring(writer, str, 0, PyUnicode_GET_LENGTH(str)): it type-checks with PyUnicode_Check (Objects/unicode_writer.c:443, accepts subclasses) and tail-calls _PyUnicodeWriter_WriteStr for the full range (Objects/unicode_writer.c:412-414), so it is behaviour-identical for three integer comparisons.

apis.name: _PyDict_GetItemStringWithError
apis.caveat: NOT a rename: the signature changes. This returns a BORROWED PyObject* (Include/cpython/dictobject.h:48); PyDict_GetItemStringRef returns an int status and writes a STRONG reference to a PyObject** out-parameter (Include/dictobject.h:68). Migration must add the out-parameter, switch to the three-state int return (-1 error / 0 absent / 1 found), and add a Py_DECREF for the new reference. A mechanical substitution does not compile.
apis.refcount_evidence: borrowed -> strong AND pointer-return -> int-status-with-outparam; arity 2 -> 3.

apis.name: _PyBytes_Resize
apis.caveat: PyBytesWriter is a different API SHAPE, not a rename: create/grow/finish instead of allocate-then-resize-in-place. Migration is per-buffer restructuring. apis.notes: Doc/whatsnew/3.15.rst, Deprecated C APIs. 30 real call sites across Objects/ + Modules/.

apis.name: PyModule_AddObject
apis.caveat: Refcount semantics differ: PyModule_AddObject steals the reference ONLY on success, so the caller must Py_DECREF on failure; PyModule_AddObjectRef never steals and PyModule_Add always steals. A mechanical rename either leaks or double-frees depending on which replacement is chosen.
apis.notes: Doc/c-api/module.rst:1022 `.. soft-deprecated:: 3.13`. Steals a reference only on success -- the replacement does not, so refcount handling must be adjusted, not just the name.

apis.name: PyErr_Fetch
apis.caveat: PyErr_Fetch returns three separate, possibly un-normalized objects; PyErr_GetRaisedException returns one normalized exception instance. Code that inspects or rebuilds the (type, value, traceback) triple has to be restructured, and a PyErr_Fetch/PyErr_Restore pair maps to GetRaisedException/SetRaisedException only when nothing in between depends on the un-normalized form.

apis.name: PyErr_Restore
apis.caveat: The mirror of PyErr_Fetch: PyErr_SetRaisedException takes a single normalized exception instance and steals it, where PyErr_Restore takes three references. Convert the fetch and the restore together.

apis.name: PyErr_NormalizeException
apis.caveat: There is no direct replacement: PyErr_GetRaisedException normalizes as part of fetching, so the correct migration deletes this call rather than renaming it.
apis.notes: Doc/c-api/exceptions.rst:567. Normalization is implicit in the raised-exception API.

apis.name: PyEval_GetBuiltins
apis.caveat: NOT a drop-in rename: the replacement returns a STRONG reference (Py_XNewRef) where this returns a BORROWED one, so a bare rename leaks the referent at every call site. Correct migration is rename + a matching Py_DECREF once the value is no longer needed. No-frame behaviour is identical (both return NULL without setting an exception), so the NULL guard needs no change.
apis.refcount_evidence: borrowed: Python/ceval.c:2633 -> _PyEval_GetBuiltins(tstate). Replacement Python/ceval.c:2881 returns Py_XNewRef(_PyEval_GetBuiltins(tstate)).

apis.name: _PyUnicodeWriter_Prepare
apis.caveat: Doc/deprecations/c-api-pending-removal-in-3.18.rst lists this with '(no replacement)'. The public PyUnicodeWriter API has no prepare step at all -- it grows on demand -- so the migration is to move the whole writer to PyUnicodeWriter_Create and drop the prepare calls, not to substitute a name.
apis.notes: MACRO form of _PyUnicodeWriter_PrepareInternal, Include/cpython/unicodeobject.h:561. The vocabulary already carries the *Internal spelling; a word-boundary matcher will not match one from the other, so both must be present -- that naming asymmetry is why ~26 call sites were invisible. The macro inlines the bounds check on the fast path and never references the marked symbol, so even an external -Wdeprecated-declarations build warns inconsistently. Sites: Objects/unicodeobject.c (x12), Objects/unicode_formatter.c (x4), Objects/longobject.c (x3), Objects/unicode_format.c, Objects/unicode_writer.c, Modules/cjkcodecs/cjkcodecs.h:166. Uses inside Objects/unicode_writer.c are the family's own implementation and are ACCEPTABLE, same as the other nine _PyUnicodeWriter_* entries.

apis.notes: Py_DEPRECATED(3.12) PyAPI_DATA at Include/cpython/pydebug.h:8; Doc/deprecations/c-api-pending-removal-in-3.16.rst, 'Global configuration variables'. 3.16 is the NEAREST removal date in this vocabulary -- nearer than the 3.18 writer family. apis.name: Py_NoSiteFlag
apis.caveat: POLARITY IS INVERTED. CPython's own bridge table says so: Python/initconfig.c maps this with GLOBAL(&Py_NoSiteFlag, 1), where the second field is literally named `not`. Py_NoSiteFlag != 0 means the behaviour is DISABLED, while PyConfig.site_import != 0 means it is ENABLED. A mechanical rename inverts the behaviour.

The vocabulary previously harvested only the *function* half of that same doc page. compat_shim_files suppresses Python/initconfig.c and Python/preconfig.c (the variables' own definitions and the PyConfig bridge -- the API's own backwards compatibility implementation) and Programs/_testembed.c (the embedding test that exercises the deprecated API on purpose, the same shape as the _testlimitedcapi trap).
